segments.speaker: God
segments.text: The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying,

segments.speaker: Ezekiel
segments.text: Now, thou son of man, take up a lamentation for Tyrus;
And say unto Tyrus,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: O thou that art situate at the entry of the sea, which art a merchant of the people for many isles, Thus saith the Lord GOD; O Tyrus, thou hast said, I am of perfect beauty.

footnotes: of perfect beauty: Heb. perfect of beauty

segments.text: Thy borders are in the midst of the seas, thy builders have perfected thy beauty.
They have made all thy ship boards of fir trees of Senir: they have taken cedars from Lebanon to make masts for thee.
Of the oaks of Bashan have they made thine oars; the company of the Ashurites have made thy benches of ivory, brought out of the isles of Chittim.

footnotes: the company…: or, they have made thy hatches of ivory well trodden

segments.text: Fine linen with broidered work from Egypt was that which thou spreadest forth to be thy sail; blue and purple from the isles of Elishah was that which covered thee.
The inhabitants of Zidon and Arvad were thy mariners: thy wise men, O Tyrus, that were in thee, were thy pilots.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: The ancients of Gebal and the wise men thereof were in thee thy calkers: all the ships of the sea with their mariners were in thee to occupy thy merchandise.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: They of Persia and of Lud and of Phut were in thine army, thy men of war: they hanged the shield and helmet in thee; they set forth thy comeliness.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: The men of Arvad with thine army were upon thy walls round about, and the Gammadims were in thy towers: they hanged their shields upon thy walls round about; they have made thy beauty perfect.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Tarshish was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of all kind of riches; with silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded in thy fairs.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they were thy merchants: they traded the persons of men and vessels of brass in thy market.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: They of the house of Togarmah traded in thy fairs with horses and horsemen and mules.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: The men of Dedan were thy merchants; many isles were the merchandise of thine hand: they brought thee for a present horns of ivory and ebony.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Syria was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of the wares of thy making: they occupied in thy fairs with emeralds, purple, and broidered work, and fine linen, and coral, and agate.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Judah, and the land of Israel, they were thy merchants: they traded in thy market wheat of Minnith, and Pannag, and honey, and oil, and balm.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Damascus was thy merchant in the multitude of the wares of thy making, for the multitude of all riches; in the wine of Helbon, and white wool.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Dan also and Javan going to and fro occupied in thy fairs: bright iron, cassia, and calamus, were in thy market.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Dedan was thy merchant in precious clothes for chariots.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Arabia, and all the princes of Kedar, they occupied with thee in lambs, and rams, and goats: in these were they thy merchants.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah, they were thy merchants: they occupied in thy fairs with chief of all spices, and with all precious stones, and gold.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Haran, and Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad, were thy merchants.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: These were thy merchants in all sorts of things, in blue clothes, and broidered work, and in chests of rich apparel, bound with cords, and made of cedar, among thy merchandise.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: The ships of Tarshish did sing of thee in thy market: and thou wast replenished, and made very glorious in the midst of the seas.
¶ Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters: the east wind hath broken thee in the midst of the seas.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Thy riches, and thy fairs, thy merchandise, thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the occupiers of thy merchandise, and all thy men of war, that are in thee, and in all thy company which is in the midst of thee, shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: The suburbs shall shake at the sound of the cry of thy pilots.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: And all that handle the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the sea, shall come down from their ships, they shall stand upon the land;

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: And shall cause their voice to be heard against thee, and shall cry bitterly, and shall cast up dust upon their heads, they shall wallow themselves in the ashes:

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: And they shall make themselves utterly bald for thee, and gird them with sackcloth, and they shall weep for thee with bitterness of heart and bitter wailing.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: And in their wailing they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and lament over thee, saying, What city is like Tyrus, like the destroyed in the midst of the sea?

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: When thy wares went forth out of the seas, thou filledst many people; thou didst enrich the kings of the earth with the multitude of thy riches and of thy merchandise.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: In the time when thou shalt be broken by the seas in the depths of the waters thy merchandise and all thy company in the midst of thee shall fall.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: All the inhabitants of the isles shall be astonished at thee, and their kings shall be sore afraid, they shall be troubled in their countenance.
The merchants among the people shall hiss at thee; thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt be any more.

footnotes: never…: Heb. shalt not be for ever
